title: Fifth thesis: between grave guilt and renewed repentance the sinner stands damnable yet to-be-absolved
source_text: XVII. Denique quibusdam in hanc sententiam interjectis, addunt Thesin istam quintam: In illo interstitio, quod est inter contractum ex gravi peccato reatum, & fidei ac poenitentiae actum renovatum, stat talis peccator, suo merito damnandus, Christi merito, & firmo Dei proposito absolvendus; non prius autem, quam per excitatam fidem ac poenitentiam veniam impetraverit, actu absolutus.
pass_a_gloss: Finally, certain things having been interposed on this opinion, they add this fifth Thesis: In that interval which is between the guilt contracted from grave sin and the renewed act of faith and repentance, such a sinner stands, by his own desert to be damned, by Christ’s merit and God’s firm purpose to be absolved; yet not actually absolved until, through faith and repentance stirred up, he has obtained pardon.
pass_b_english: Between grave guilt and renewed faith-repentance the sinner stands damnable by desert.
Christ’s merit and God’s purpose mark him for absolution—but not actually absolved until pardon is sought in living faith.

lemmas.gloss: to be damned by his own desert
